summary: This Wikipedia article on Hyderabad covers the city's transport (buses, MMTS suburban rail, Hyderabad Metro plans), media and internet history, health statistics from the 2005 National Family Health Survey, and its history from Qutb Shahi and Nizam rule through British alliance and Indian union. It also describes the naming theories, economic development, vehicle and traffic figures, and the municipal and metropolitan administrative structure (GHMC, Secunderabad Cantonment Board, HMDA).
one_line: Overview of Hyderabad, India, covering its transport, media, health, history, naming, economy, traffic, and governance.
key_facts: Bus services operate from the Mahatma Gandhi Bus Station in the city centre and carry over 130 million passengers daily.
The Multi-Modal Transport System (MMTS) is a three line suburban rail service used by over 160,000 passengers daily.
Secunderabad Railway Station is the largest intercity rail station in Hyderabad and serves as headquarters of Indian Railways' South Central Railway zone.
Doordarshan began television broadcasting in Hyderabad in 1974; private satellite channels started in July 1992 with the launch of Star TV.
The first public internet access service in Hyderabad began in 1995, and the first private ISP started operations in 1998.
The 2005 National Family Health Survey reported a city total fertility rate of 1.8, and an infant mortality rate of 35 per 1,000 live births.
In 1798 the Nizam signed a subsidiary alliance with the East India Company, allowing the British Indian Army to occupy Bolarum (modern Secunderabad).
Hyderabad became the formal capital of the Nizams in 1769.
Hyderabad means 'Haydar's city' or 'lion city', named to honour the Caliph Ali Ibn Abi Talib, also known as Haydar.
Hyderabad was established in 1591 by Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah and was ruled by the Qutb Shahi dynasty for nearly a century before the Mughals captured the region.
In 1724 Mughal viceroy Asif Jah I declared sovereignty and created the Nizams of Hyderabad dynasty.
The Greater Hyderabad Municipal Corporation (GHMC) was formed in April 2007 by merging the Municipal Corporation of Hyderabad with 12 municipalities covering 650 km2.
As of 2012 there were over 3.5 million vehicles in the city, 74% of which were two-wheelers.
The Hyderabad Elevated Expressway is described as the longest flyover in India.
In 2014 Telangana split from Andhra Pradesh and Hyderabad became joint capital of the two states, a transitional arrangement scheduled to end by 2025.
